newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish jewellers hail govt plan to register gold.
newsitem.headline: Turkish jewellers hail govt plan to register gold.

text.p: Turkish jewellers strongly support a government plan to have unregistered physical inventories of precious metals, mainly gold, declared.

"We fully support this plan. Actually, it is the outcome of our comprehensive report which was sent to the Prime Ministry 1-1/2 month ago," Mustafa Oztepe, president of the jewellers association, said on Thursday.

Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan who unveiled his government's second revenue-raising package today, said jewellers who declare unregistered precious metal, diamond and jewellery inventories will pay only a four percent fine.
The government expects to raise 34 trillion lira and bring out some 700 tonnes of unregistered precious metals held by jewellers.
Erbakan said the state would earn an additional 30 trillion lira from related income taxes on newly declared stocks.
Oztepe said around 47,000 jewellers in the sector had been awaiting an official call to declare their unregistered, thus illegal, physical inventories which he put at 720 tonnes.
The sector also wants the government to allow future appreciation in the value of newly declared inventories to be recorded as capital increases, Oztepe added.
